event.details: Pṛthu teaches dharma and rules happily, described as Viṣṇu-form/equal prowess. Four Sanaka-led sons of Brahmā, ever child-aged, radiant and delusion-free, visit. Pṛthu rises, prostrates head at feet, worships with footwater/arghya/seats and massages their feet. He praises land/city/home/lineage/parents/learning/tapas as fortunate through visit, attributes sight to earlier merit, and asks their instructions. No guessed new parental genealogy from his praise.

event.details: Pleased by humility, Kumāras say they desire no task and are naked, have come because they heard king’s fame in heaven, and ask permission to return Brahmaloka. Pṛthu says he has enjoyed kingdom/varied pleasures and now asks yoga for peace. Recognizing qualification/disenchantment, they teach that full Gaṇeśa yoga-peace is to be worshipped with great devotion for peace. This is teacher exchange, not a direct new Gaṇeśa appearance.

event.details: Kumāras recount earlier visiting Śiva seated meditating beneath banyan at his abode. They bow and awaken him with hymns; ending meditation he says salutation to Gaṇeśa. Astonished, they ask who Gaṇādhipa is and why supposedly independent sahaja Śiva bows. Śiva joyfully explains primordial Gaṇapatya peace-knowledge. These are recollection inside Pṛthu teaching, not simultaneous Śiva visit to king.

event.details: In recollection Śiva questions independent sahaja versus dependent threefold categories in Veda-described Brahman, and calls varied karma/yoga/knowledge forms māyā-associated. Union of actions is action-Brahman, similarly knowledge-Brahman. Gaṇa means group, union of external/internal differences; food/prāṇa and other Brahman-denoting words are gaṇas and Gaṇeśvara their lord. He is yoga of union/ayoga and all yogas; Śiva and others are his yoga-form gaṇas and bow. Māyā is obstacle/reflection-delusion, overcome by Vighnarāja service; Gaṇapatya yogins become Brahman. Śiva declares Gaṇeśa-form identity and difference as māyā. Claims attributed to recalled Śiva speech.

event.details: Śiva identifies fivefold mind as varied Buddhi, and sovereignty there as Siddhi. Gaṇeśa reflection amid two māyās is deluded; abandon reflected state/fivefold mind through Gaṇeśa service to become Cintāmaṇi. He questions operation of union and yoga in Gaṇeśa-identity, affirms nondifference and yoga-peace/Brahman attainment, and calls this his secret meditation, why he is Gaṇeśa’s servant and bows. Kumāras say doubt ended; they now wander Earth/heavens/nether hollows as Gaṇapatya yogins. Buddhi/Siddhi here are philosophical personifications, not new biological spouses or marriage scene.

event.details: Kumāras fall silent/prostrate; devotion-bound child Vināyaka says hymn gives yoga-peace to readers/hearers and he will give the desired object while himself moved by the hymn; Kumāras will become Gaṇapatyas like Śiva. No request words or Pṛthu-directed boon here. Child then plays with children like ordinary child. Kumāras visit Kāśī king, are honored, eat and return to their place. They conclude Pṛthu should worship Gaṇeśa as full peace-knowledge.

event.details: Kumāras return Brahmā’s world. Pṛthu divides kingdom among UNNAMED SONS(plural) and goes forest. Following yoga progression he becomes Gaṇapatya; at end humble king WITH WIFE merges in Gaṇeśa. The wife is unnamed, not remembered Arci. Hearing/reading Pṛthu account gives all. Actual merger is distinct from embedded Vināyaka promise to Kumāras.
event.outcome: Pṛthu and wife actually merge in Gaṇeśa after forest practice.
